outcomes.description: Paper is stuffed into the cup.
outcomes.target: The paper is visibly placed inside the cup, with evidence that it has been stuffed into it rather than merely resting nearby or on its rim.
outcomes.reference: The requested edit is stated in the instruction: “Stuffing the paper into the cup”.

nodes.question: What paper and receiving objects are visibly present in the source and edited images, and does direct feature comparison establish whether an edited receiving object is a cup?
nodes.criteria: Pass if the images permit a grounded inventory and comparison, even if a particular identity remains unresolved. Separately report source paper and cup identification, edited paper and cup identification, and source-to-edit correspondence as established, disproved, or unresolved, with visible reasons. Inventory pass does not establish cup identity or insertion. Fail if adequate edited-image visibility positively establishes absence of the paper or any relevant receiving object. Unknown if visibility prevents a grounded inventory. A source cup does not by itself establish an edited cup, and unresolved correspondence does not prove removal.
nodes.binding: Inspect both images directly. First identify objects from visible structure in each image; then compare candidate counterparts using contour, proportions, opening or rim structure, enclosing walls, orientation, and other distinctive features that are actually visible. Allow source evidence to inform identity when supported by edited-image correspondence, but do not transfer source geometry into an occluded edit. Test retention, alteration, replacement, and unresolved correspondence without presupposing any of them. A color change alone neither establishes nor disproves cup identity. Describe edited paper boundaries, candidate receiving-object boundaries, overlap, and precisely which regions are obscured. Do not demand a visible interior as the sole identity test, infer insertion from a hand grip, or infer any object from the instruction alone.

nodes.question: Within s1's inventory, does direct inspection establish paper entry or intermediate stuffing into a cup, establish wholly external placement without requested progress, or leave the decisive relation obscured?
nodes.criteria: Pass if grounded paper-and-cup identity and positive geometry establish entry, containment, or insertion-related deformation at the receiving opening; distinguish intermediate progress from potentially completed stuffing. Fail if affirmative spatial evidence establishes that the relevant paper remains wholly external, is merely on the rim without stuffing action, or a required object is demonstrably absent under adequate visibility. External-placement failure need not establish the candidate object's identity: it requires traceable paper boundaries or free endpoints and occlusion ordering sufficient to exclude entry, plus inspection of other possible receiving objects and relevant hidden regions. Lack of a visible opening, unresolved correspondence, a non-cup hypothesis, or absence of positive insertion cues alone is insufficient for fail. Unknown if a hidden paper segment, contact boundary, or uncertain receiver identity leaves actual cup entry and external placement indistinguishable. Report identity, spatial relation, progress, and decisive visibility separately.
nodes.binding: Use s1 as coarse ancestor context, not as a spatial conclusion. Inspect the edited image directly and trace the paper perimeter, especially free corners and edges nearest each candidate receiver. State which edges visibly terminate, continue across a foreground surface, or disappear behind an enclosing boundary. Test whether the paper occludes the candidate or the candidate occludes the paper, and whether that ordering resolves interior versus exterior placement. Check whether any visible curved line is an opening boundary or merely a surface marking; do not assume either. Distinguish an obscured object's boundary from an obscured paper-entry boundary: the former does not automatically make progress unknown, while the latter may. Inspect the rest of the scene and hand-covered regions for alternative entry paths. A free visible corner alone cannot exclude insertion elsewhere; identify the scope of each cue and any genuinely unresolved segment. Do not invent hidden insertion or dismiss plausible insertion supported by actual occlusion geometry. Source correspondence may inform identity but cannot establish edited entry. Do not count a grip, printing change, or mere proximity as stuffing.

nodes.question: Given the inventory and nested entry investigation, does the edited image establish completed stuffing, established incompleteness, or unresolved completion?
nodes.criteria: Pass only if grounded paper-and-cup identity and concrete containment, insertion, or compression establish completed stuffing; some paper may remain outside. Fail if affirmative evidence establishes incomplete insertion, wholly external placement, rim-only placement without stuffing, or adequately visible absence of a required object. A grounded demonstration that the paper has not entered any receiver can establish noncompletion even when the nearby candidate's identity is unresolved. Separately report whether noncompletion coexists with positive insertion progress or established no progress. Unknown if the spatial relation remains undecidable, or if positive entry is present but cup identity or completed stuffing remains unresolved. Completion failure alone does not determine progress.
nodes.binding: Use s1 and s4_opening_entry in saved order as ancestor context, then independently inspect the edited image for containment and stuffing extent. Reconcile conflicts through explicit visible boundaries and occlusion evidence. Do not convert s1's inventory pass into cup identity or s4_opening_entry's progress pass into completion. Conversely, do not require receiver identity to reject completion when verified external placement already excludes insertion. Preserve uncertainty where an actual hidden entry path or incomplete-versus-complete distinction cannot be resolved. Do not demand unchanged source color, infer an unseen interior, or count unrelated changes as progress.

nodes.question: Does the image show the paper stuffed inside the cup?
nodes.criteria: Use all and only s1, s4_opening_entry, and s2 observations in that order; interpret their evidence, not merely their statuses. Complete requires established paper-and-cup identity, positive cup-entry evidence from s4_opening_entry, and completed contained stuffing from s2. Partial requires positively established entry or intermediate stuffing into a cup from s4_opening_entry and positively established incompleteness from s2. Absent requires affirmative no-progress evidence from s4_opening_entry, corroborated or reconciled by s2: adequately demonstrated wholly external placement, rim-only placement without stuffing action, or adequately visible absence of a required object. Uncertain candidate identity or source correspondence does not defeat absent when trustworthy spatial evidence already excludes requested entry, but neither uncertainty nor missing positive cues supplies that exclusion. Unknown applies when evidence necessary for the applicable conclusion remains unresolved, or support observations conflict without grounded resolution. Failure of s2 alone never establishes absent. s1's pass supplies inventory context only; dependent support agreement is not independent confirmation. Do not infer visual facts or award completion credit to supporting checks.

program.checker_template:
Execute ONE saved check. Return status, evidence, confidence (0 to 1 or null), and used_dependency_ids. You receive no reference label or optimizer feedback. Do not predict what the optimizer wants.
Support checks receive source and edited images. Inspect only the saved visual proposition and binding. When dependencies are supplied, use those ancestor observations as context and investigate the more specific proposition yourself; do not simply repeat the parent answer. Use pass/fail/unknown. A pass on a broad parent does not imply a nested check passes. Known negative evidence is usable; uncertain or missing evidence is unknown. Do not award requested completion credit to supporting facts.
The requested fulfillment readout receives NO images. Use ALL and ONLY saved support observations, the original instruction, rubric and saved composition criteria. Use complete/partial/absent/unknown. Mere texture or object presence must not silently establish whole-image conversion or a requested spatial relation. Known progress plus evidenced incompleteness may be partial; absence means no requested progress. Missing necessary evidence is unknown, never a fabricated failure or completion. Do not infer new visual facts.
used_dependency_ids must name every supplied dependency check_id exactly once in saved order (empty when none). Confidence is self-report, not calibrated correctness.

observations.evidence: Source: a large white sheet of paper is visible beside a blue cylindrical cup lying on its side; the cup has a broad circular rim/opening and enclosing walls. Edited: a blue printed paper/card is held in a hand, with its boundaries visible except where covered by the fingers; a pink rounded object with a dark curved line is behind it. The edited image does not visibly establish that this rounded object is a cup: its rim/opening and enclosing walls are not discernible. The edited paper's appearance and shape differ from the source sheet, and no distinctive correspondence is established. Thus source paper and cup are identified; edited paper is identified, edited cup identity and source-to-edit correspondence are unresolved. The edited paper overlaps and obscures part of the pink object, while the hand obscures part of the paper.

The edited image shows a blue printed paper/card held in a hand overlapping a pink rounded object. The paper’s visible edges appear to lie across the object, but the object’s identity as a cup and any opening or enclosing boundary are not established. The hand also obscures part of the paper, so the decisive entry relation cannot be resolved; neither insertion nor wholly external placement is established.

Edited: a blue-and-white printed paper/card is held in a hand, with its boundaries visible; behind it is a reddish rounded object with a dark curved line, but the paper and hand obscure much of that object's contour. The images allow a grounded inventory and comparison, so the inventory criterion passes; this does not establish insertion.

The paper’s visible edges appear to remain outside the object, but the object’s identity and opening are not established, and the hand obscures the relevant contact area. Thus the image does not resolve whether paper is entering a cup or remains wholly external. The ancestor inventory observation provides context but does not establish entry.

findings.source_phrase: Stuffing the paper into the cup
findings.question: Does direct inspection of the edited image establish that the paper is wholly outside the reddish object, or does the hand/object overlap conceal a possible entry path?
findings.criteria: Trace the paper edges and their occlusion against the object, including the hand-covered contact area. Establish no progress only if visible geometry excludes entry; otherwise retain uncertainty. Do not infer cup identity from the object’s rounded shape.
findings.evidence: The edited image shows a hand holding a printed paper/card across a reddish rounded object. The paper overlaps the object, while the hand covers part of the contact region; the visible image does not clearly show an opening or enclosing rim.
findings.rationale: The saved entry check reports unknown, but its evidence does not detail whether the visible edge and overlap geometry affirmatively rules out entry or leaves a specific entry path obscured. That distinction is necessary to separate no progress from unresolved evidence; the broad inventory pass does not settle it.

findings.source_phrase: Stuffing the paper into the cup
findings.question: Does the edited image show any paper entering or being compressed into a receiving opening, and, if so, is that receiver visibly identifiable as a cup?
findings.criteria: Assess the edited image’s visible opening/rim, enclosing walls, paper boundaries, and their occlusion relation. Count progress only with positive evidence of entry or insertion-related deformation into a cup; proximity, overlap, or a hand grip alone is insufficient. If the relevant boundary is obscured or cup identity remains unresolved, report that uncertainty.
findings.evidence: The edited image shows a printed paper/card held in front of a reddish rounded object with a dark curved line. No clear cup rim/opening or enclosing walls are visible, and the hand and paper obscure part of the object.
findings.rationale: The existing entry observation is unknown and the completion check was not executed because of a dependency failure. A focused direct check of positive entry and receiver identity would address the central requested relation without treating transport/schema failures as visual evidence.
